%CHANGE.comment: From 20 to 50 is a rise of 150 percent

Ans.comment: Ans is the 42 from the line above, so the second line adds 1 to it

ARG.comment: The angle mode is degrees: (1,1) lies at 45 degrees

COLNORM.comment: Stores a 2 by 2 matrix in M1; its columns sum to 4 and 6 in absolute value

ROWNORM.comment: Stores a 2 by 2 matrix in M1; its rows sum to 3 and 7 in absolute value

COND.comment: The column norm 2 times that of the inverse, 1, gives 2

COT.comment: The angle mode is degrees, so 1 means 1 degree

CSC.comment: The angle mode is degrees, so 1 means 1 degree

CROSS.comment: M1 and M2 hold the x and y unit vectors; their cross product is the z unit vector

EIGENVAL.comment: The eigenvalues of a diagonal matrix are its diagonal entries

FLOOR.comment: A negative value rounds down, away from zero

FNROOT.comment: Finds where X^2-2 is zero, starting the search at X = 1: the square root of 2

IFTE.comment: The test 1 is non-zero, so the result is the second argument, 5

ITERATE.comment: Squares X three times from the start value 2: 4, 16, 256

MAKELIST.comment: A^2 for A from 1 to 4 in steps of 1

MAKEMAT.comment: A 2 by 2 matrix whose entry is row I plus column J

NTHROOT.comment: The cube root of 8; the degree 3 comes first

POLYCOEF.comment: The roots 2 and -3 give X^2 + X - 6

POS.comment: The 12 is the 3rd element of the list

QUAD.comment: Solves X^2 - 4 = 0; s1*4/2 stands for 2 and -2

RANK.comment: The second row is twice the first, so the rank is 1

RREF.comment: Stores an augmented matrix in M1; the last column holds the solution x = -1, y = 2

UTPN.comment: Mean 0, variance 1, at the value 0: half of the probability lies above

∂.comment: Differentiates s1^2+3*s1 with respect to s1; the name s1 keeps the result symbolic

∫.comment: The area under 2*X from X = 0 to X = 1
